label: text
text: M. Poincare to-day is submitting to the Cabinet his scheme for the organisation of a sinking fund for National Defence. Bonds and Treasury Bonds of a minimum term of one year.

label: text
text: In order to give this fund an effective guaranteed and make it independent of party politics, laws instituting it will be embodied in

label: text
text: the constitution. for which purpose the National Assembly, consisting of the Chamber and Senate as one body, is to be convoked at Versailles to sanction the necessary modification of the constitution.

label: text
text: This National Assembly, apart from regular meetings for the election of the President, of the Republic, has only twice been specially convoked—once in 1879, to provide for the transfer of Parliament from Versailles to Paris, and in 1882, to modify the organisation of the Senate.—Reuter.

label: text
text: M. Poincare will lay to-day before the Council of Ministers' his plan for a sinking fund for National Defence Bonds and Treasury Bonds, issued for periods of less than a year. The plan will give definite shape to the Government's expressed intention to conform to all undertakings entered into by the State towards its creditors, and will show that the Government does not contemplate forced consolidation of bonds.

label: text
text: M. Poincare will confer with a committee of experts as to stabilizing the france.

label: text
text: As soon as "the Finance Bill has passed the Senate, M. Poincare will begin to exchange views with Parliamentary committees concerning the war debts "settlements.—Havas."

label: text
text:
The Cabinet has approved of M. Poincare's Sinking Fund scheme, also his project for the commercialisation of the tobacco monopoly.
—Reuter.

label: text
text: The franc on London is quoted at 185.—Reuter.

label: text
text: The Senate Finance Committee as adopted all the articles in the government's financial proposals—Reuter.

label: text
text: Le Matin learns from Geneva that Mr. Mellon spent yesterday there, and, interviewed, said when he left Washington he intended holidaying in Europe, but a cable gram from President Coolidge made him work.

label: text
text: He had already discussed financial matters in Paris, and he was going to Rome to-day, when finance would again occupy his attention.—Reuter.

label: text
text: Delegates of various colonial societies, including the naval and army association of Tsingtau and cagnate African unions, assembled for the opening of the German Colonial Congress, otherwise known as the Korag.

label: text
text: The President, welcoming the delegates, expressed confidence in the success of the second campaign now in preparation aiming at a return of Germany's former colonial possessions.—Reuter.

label: text
text: Lieut.-Commander W. A. Higgins, captain of H.M.S. Teal, died at Shanghai to-day, aged 33. He is a victim of the recent hext-wave.—Reutor.

label: text
text:
Mexico City, August 2.
The British Minister, Mr. Ovey.
has made representations to the
Mexican Foreign Office on behalf
of the Anglican Cathedral, which
is British privately owned but is
under jurisdiction of the American
Episcopal Church.

label: text
text: Mr. Ovey has been instructed to protest against its possible seizure under the religious law now enforced, specifying that all churches are the property of the nation.

label: text
text: It is understood the Archbishop of Canterbury has taken a leading part in requesting the British Foreign Office's intervention.

label: text
text: The Mexican Foreign Office has replied that the case will be carefully considered.

label: text
text: Dean Peacock a British ex-army chaplain, was recently arrested and charged with violating the religious laws, and his case is subjudice.

label: text
text: The Dean conducted Communion services at his residence, which is not regarded as a violation of the law.

label: text
text: The Catholic Episcopate has made a statement as to its willingness to enter into a truce with the Government for a reasonable length of time, until the people by a plebisseite. Decide regarding the religious controversy, and suggests in the meantime a suspension of persecution.

label: text
text: Yesterday's labour parade was in favour of the Government's standpoint. While the demonstrators "were passing the palace of President Calles the Ministers stood quiet.

label: text
text: Catholics knelt in the priestlies churches, praying for the improvement of the situation.

label: text
text: The economic boycott has had a marked effect in some parts of the country.

label: text
text: Catholics are wearing mourning, and their houses are draped with crepe.—Reuter's American Service.

label: text
text:
Mexico City, August 2.
A policeman was killed last night by a stone thrown by a woman among a crowd around a church.
Another policeman wounded a woman, who subsequently died.

label: text
text: The crowd later collided with troops, who fired a volley, wounding nine persons.

label: text
text: The crowds, thronging the churches at Pachuca for the closing services on Sunday were so dense that six women and six children were suffocated.

label: text
text: Fifty thousand persons took part in a procession in Mexico City to day in support of the Government's policy.

label: text
text: The usual Sunday bull fight was crowded, and everything was fairly quiet, but there was a general under-current of excitement. —Router

label: text
text: A protest on general of the church owned by the United States is made by the American Consul-General to the State Department in Washington against the Mexican Government taking over the Episcopul Church at San Jose de Gracia, the deeds of which are held by the Episcopal headquarters in New York City.

label: text
text: The Mexican authorities say that the property was taken over because the rector failed to register and give the required information under the new regulations.—Router.

label: text
text: San Francisco, July 26.—The federal grand jury to-day returned an indictment containing 11 counts against Colonel Ned M. Green; prohibition administrator for Northern California, charging embezzlement of government property. The jury was in session only three and a half hours. All of the counts relate to the alleged appropriation of seized liquor for his own use. Colonel Green filed a bond of $6,000.

label: text
text: Accompanied by Government exports a small Commission of employers' and workers' representatives is to be sent to the United States to study industrial relationships there.

label: text
text: The idea is believed to have originated with Sir Arthur Steel-Maitland, Minister of Labour, and has since received Cabinet approval.

label: text
text: With the navy demanding continuous appropriation of about $150,000,000 for the construction of auxiliary ships between now and 1931, when the replacement of battleships may begin under the terms of the Washington treaty, the army has formally applied for a big increase in their annual appropriations.

label: text
text: It is understood that the pre-mier and minister of finance view the new development with satisfaction. In view of the fact that the navy was certain to be refused, they feel it will be easier to refuse both army and navy than either one alone.

label: text
text: It is probable that the navy will be voted between $15,000,-000 and $25,000,000 for construction next year, but not as part of the appropriation they are asking for.—United Press.

text:
The total of last week's ruffings casualties is now put down at 126 deaths, 400 missing, 100 boats sunk, of which 60 were in harbour, and $8,000,000 damage to property.
The sponge fleet did not suffer so much as was at first feared, only 80 out of 400 boats having gone to the sponge banks when the storm broke. All these are believed to be lost, with 350 men forming the crews.—Reuter's American Service.
